first.rationale: We face concurrent drops in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ), signaling a funnel problem at the earliest stages. Memory_31 and memory_86 both document that onboarding simplification and completion improvements drive durable activation lift in self-serve SMB cohorts—precisely where the competitor is most threatening. Promotional pricing alone would be reactive and commoditizing; referral incentives require healthy activation as a prerequisite; enterprise sales assist is orthogonal to the current activation decay. We are verifying memory_31 (signup simplification) and memory_91 (activation messaging) to confirm the relative magnitudes of lift and determine if a combined or sequential approach is warranted. A standard_experiment targeting simplified onboarding lets us diagnose whether the funnel pressure is field-count friction or deeper product-readiness issues, and positions us to recover qualified volume in the SMB segment under competitive pressure. This preserves the enterprise sales assist option as a follow-up if needed.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms both signup simplification (+15% signup, +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue on SMB) and in-product activation messaging (+11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, +1% retention lift) are reliable levers. Given the current 6% activation drop and 4% onboarding completion decline, simplifying onboarding addresses the immediate funnel degradation with the strongest documented effect size (+9% activation, +4% qualified revenue). This is the highest-leverage single intervention available. The modest -1% retention risk from exp_31 is acceptable given the qualified revenue lift and the current competitive pressure on price-sensitive SMB accounts. A standard experiment allows us to validate that the original effect still holds under current market conditions while preserving the option to layer activation messaging (exp_91) in a follow-up cycle if needed. This approach maximizes sustainable qualified revenue by restoring funnel health in our most threatened segment.

final2.rationale: The competitive landscape has shifted materially. Doubled churn conversations with price-sensitive SMB accounts now represent an immediate revenue-defense crisis that outweighs the funnel optimization strategy. Memory_73 documents that targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. While simplifying onboarding remains a high-confidence intervention for activation recovery, it operates on a multi-week cycle and cannot arrest active churn this week. A small_guarded_test of promotional pricing allows us to: (1) immediately signal competitive response to at-risk accounts, (2) preserve margin by targeting price-sensitive cohorts rather than broad-based discounting, (3) gather win/loss data on which accounts are price-elastic vs. value-motivated, and (4) maintain the onboarding simplification experiment in parallel for next cycle. Risk flagged: aggressive pricing can commoditize perception and constrain future margin recovery; we mitigate by keeping scope guarded and time-bound. This preserves uncertainty about optimal long-term positioning while addressing the acute retention threat.
